title: Peddi Has Crossed ₹112 Crore Worldwide on Day One. Ram Charan Just Delivered the Biggest Telugu Opening of 2026.
excerpt: With ₹51 crore net in India and $1 million in North American premieres nearly locked, Buchi Babu Sana's sports drama has outpaced Pathaan, Raja Saab, and every Telugu opener this year. The Hindi belt, though, is a different story.
body:
Ram Charan's Peddi has opened with the kind of numbers that settle arguments before they start. Buchi Babu Sana's rural sports drama collected ₹51 crore net in India on its first day across 12,412 shows, with paid preview screenings on June 3 pushing the combined domestic total to ₹69.50 crore net. The worldwide gross stands at ₹112.49 crore, making it comfortably the biggest Telugu opener of 2026 and Ram Charan's best since RRR.

## The Telugu Belt Carried the Film

The Telugu version was the engine behind the opening. It earned ₹47.20 crore net on Day 1 alone, with Andhra Pradesh and Telangana contributing ₹48 crore to the gross. Occupancy in Telugu markets reached 67.92 percent overall, climbing to 76.69 percent by the evening shows. Karnataka added ₹5.75 crore. Tamil Nadu and Kerala combined for under ₹2 crore, which is expected for a Telugu-first film without a prior pan-India franchise.

The numbers put Peddi ahead of some formidable recent openers. It has outpaced Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar (₹30 crore Day 1), Shah Rukh Khan's Pathaan (₹57 crore), and Prabhas's The Raja Saab (₹62 crore) in domestic collections. Only Dhurandhar 2's extraordinary ₹102 crore opening remains out of reach.

## Hindi Collections Are a Concern

The one soft spot is the Hindi belt. Peddi earned ₹3 crore net in Hindi on Day 1, roughly half of what NTR Jr's Devara managed in its Hindi version. For a ₹350-crore production that marketed itself as a pan-India event, that number is a warning. Mixed early reviews, particularly criticism of narrative pacing and Janhvi Kapoor's performance, appear to have suppressed Hindi walk-ins. Critics have been consistent on one point: Ram Charan's intensity is the film's anchor, but the writing around him is uneven.

## North America Is Tracking Toward $1 Million in Premieres

The overseas market contributed ₹30 crore in gross. In North America specifically, Peddi was just $130,000 short of crossing $1 million in premiere pre-sales before opening day, according to tracking by Venky Box Office. It sold 28,037 tickets across 533 locations and 1,647 shows in the United States alone. Cinemark emerged as the biggest contributor with $466,707 from 16,344 tickets, followed by Regal at $160,766.

The premium format push is notable. Nearly $280,000 came from XD, RPX, D-Box, and other PLF screens, a trend usually associated with major Hollywood tentpoles. Telugu films have steadily built this infrastructure over the past three years, and Peddi is the latest beneficiary.

## What the Diaspora Needs to Know

For NRIs who follow Telugu cinema, the opening signals that the theatrical experience around Indian films in North America has genuinely matured. The days of hunting for a single screen in a 50-mile radius are over. Peddi screened in 533 locations across the US on premiere night, a distribution footprint that would have been unthinkable five years ago.

The film itself draws from director Buchi Babu Sana's own village, inspired by a real labourer named Peddi Raju who was so talented at cricket and basketball that rival teams reportedly paid him to play for their side. Set in rural Uttarandhra in the 1980s, it features Ram Charan, Janhvi Kapoor, Shiva Rajkumar, Jagapathi Babu, Divyenndu, and Boman Irani, with music by AR Rahman.

## The Road to Profitability

At ₹350 crore production budget, Peddi needs sustained collections to break even. The Telugu belt is delivering. The Hindi belt is not, at least not yet. Whether word-of-mouth can lift Hindi numbers over the weekend will determine if this is a blockbuster or merely a big opening. The next 48 hours are the test.

Netflix has secured post-theatrical streaming rights, but no OTT date has been announced. For now, Peddi is a theatrical event, and on Day 1, the theaters showed up.
